subject: SIG questionnaire — hosting mode clarifications and evidence pack for BigBank
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@bigbank.com>

Cc: compliance-team@bigbank.com

Subject: SIG questions: hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private) and evidence request

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this on. BigBank's SIG review returned a set of follow-up questions specifically about how Redwood's different hosting options map to SIG controls (Q12-Q17). The reviewers want explicit statements and supporting evidence around:

- Where customer data is processed/stored for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (data residency guarantees).
- Tenant isolation boundaries for Dedicated vs Hosted (multi-tenant vs single-tenant).
- KMS / BYOK support and key custody model for each mode.
- Network isolation / VPC connectivity patterns and egress control examples.
- Audit logging (what is captured, retention, and access model).
- SOC 2 scope coverage and how it applies to each deployment mode.

Can you send a short mapping (one page preferred) that we can attach to the SIG response and any supporting artifacts (network diagram, KMS flow, SOC 2 scope excerpt)? The review team would like the materials by Aug 20 so they can finish our submission.

If there's an existing pack, please share. If we need a quick call to clarify scope, note availability.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Information Security Manager — Third-Party Risk
BigBank Inc

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@bigbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questions: hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private) and evidence request

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. I put together a concise mapping and attached an "answer pack" that addresses each SIG item and points to evidence files. Summary below (short, for the SIG):

1) Hosted (Redwood Cloud — multi-tenant service)
- Data processing & storage: Customer workloads run on shared clusters in our managed cloud regions. Customers can request region restrictions where available; we publish region availability per model.
- Isolation: Logical tenant isolation (namespaces, per-tenant KV cache separation, network ACLs). No dedicated GPUs per customer in the standard hosted tier.
- Keys: Provider-managed encryption keys by default; we offer managed customer KMS integration for specific enterprise agreements (limited BYOK options).
- Network: Outbound egress controlled via provider network policies. No customer-controlled VPC peering.
- Audit logs & SOC 2: Audit logs captured centrally; SOC 2 in-scope for the hosted control plane and shared runtime. Retention options are available as an add-on.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity pools)
- Data processing & storage: Dedicated GPU pools logically reserved for the customer. Data remains in the same cloud region but runs on capacity not shared with other tenants.
- Isolation: Single-tenant serving pools, isolated customer namespaces, and optional dedicated subnetting.
- Keys: BYOK supported via customer-managed cloud KMS integration (customer supplies KMS keys or grants access as part of onboarding); see attached "kms_keyflow_dedicated.pdf" for end-to-end flow.
- Network: Optional VPC peering or private connectivity; egress routes can be restricted to customer-managed endpoints.
- Audit logs & SOC 2: Dedicated capacity nodes are covered by our SOC 2 scope; logs can be routed to the customer's logging collection (S3/CloudWatch) per configuration.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Data processing & storage: Deployed into customer-owned VPCs or on-prem hardware; customer controls physical location.
- Isolation: Full tenancy within customer network boundary; Redwood control plane can be deployed as a SaaS-managed control plane or as a private control plane (enterprise option).
- Keys: Full BYOK/HSM options; customers can keep keys entirely on-prem or in their KMS.
- Network: Customer controls all ingress/egress; typical pattern is VPC peering, private endpoints, with explicit firewall rules.
- Audit logs & SOC 2: For private/on-prem we provide audit tooling and can include evidence of configuration; SOC 2 applicability depends on deployment model and contract (we provide attestation artifacts when Redwood-managed components are in-scope).

Attachments included: redwood_sig_answer_pack_v1.pdf (answers mapped to SIG question IDs), network_diagram_private_vpc.png (example topology), kms_keyflow_dedicated.pdf (technical key flow).

Next steps:
- I've cc'd Marissa for the SOC 2 excerpt and to confirm retention windows.
- If the reviewers want a one-page table that maps specific SIG question IDs to the evidence file names, I can add that as a supplement.

Would you like a short 30-minute walkthrough before Aug 20? We're free Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG questions: hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private) and evidence request — KMS / BYOK details

Hi Sarah — quick technical clarification on keys and custody across the three modes (pulling out the KMS-specific questions):

- Hosted: Default is provider-managed keys (encrypted-at-rest with keys we manage). For enterprise customers we can offer a managed KMS integration where customer-provided cloud KMS keys are used to wrap service-level keys; this is subject to contract and may have limitations on historic data rewrapping. Hosted BYOK is available for select enterprise accounts (we will document the exact contract addendum).

- Dedicated: Native support for customer-managed keys. Typical pattern: customer creates a key in their cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS), grants Redwood a ciphertext-encrypt/decrypt IAM role for the specific key, and Redwood's serving nodes use envelope encryption so raw keys never leave KMS. Attached is "kms_keyflow_dedicated.pdf" showing the envelope encryption lifecycle and key rotation recommendations.

- Private / On-prem: Customers can keep full custody — we support HSM integrations (PKCS#11) and on-prem KMS. In scenarios where Redwood manages a private control plane, we recommend a customer-managed HSM for key custody; documentation for HSM integration is included in the answer pack.

Auditing: For Dedicated and Private we can provide KMS usage logs (CloudTrail events or HSM audit logs) as evidence. For Hosted, we provide KMS access logs where applicable and service-level audit records.

If compliance needs a test plan (sample CloudTrail extracts, log formats), we can produce a redacted sample set.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Security Engineer — Cryptography & Key Management
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms_keyflow_dedicated.pdf
